Ich habe Shadow of the Colossos als Kind geliebt und hatte Praey for the Gods schon seit Ewigkeiten auf meiner Wunschliste, weil ich gar nicht wirklich geschaut habe was es genau für ein Game ist bis ich es jetzt doch endlich mal gekauft habe und ich hab es keine Sekunde bereut.

Es sieht wirklich schön aus und lief durchgehend flüssig. das Setting kann eventuell etwas eintönig werden aber mir hat es wirklich gut gefallen durch die verschneiten Ruinen zu traben und allerlei dinge dazwischen zu finden. Wie schon zu anfang erwähnt liebe ich Shadow of the colossos weil es eine Kindheitserinnerung von mir ist und dieses Spiel hat jede Sekunde davon perfekt eingefangen. Die Bosse sind alle wirklich schön und abwechslungsreich, auch wenn manche ziemlich einfach waren. Habe auf Normal gespielt und nur den Survival Aspekt auf schwer gestellt, hatte aber nie wirkliche Probleme. 
Ich kanndas Spiel also wirklich nur empfehlen, wenn man SotC schon gut fand damals.

This was purely a game to ride off of Shadow of the Colossus. It's sad to see that it went the way of a basic :Run around and find resources" simulator rather than an actual game. I could not recommend it in good faith.

Mechanically the game is a little bit clunky, but the concept is great.
You can max it in 25h, before the constant struggles with survival aspects will tire you out.

Praey for the Gods is a decent game about exploration, survival, puzzle solving and climbing (the main way you fight the bosses). I hated the survival aspects and turned them off immediately. Other than that I enjoyed what the game had to offer. The bosses in particular were quite interesting and unique. In my opinion the price is a bit steep for the length and play style so I would recommend getting it during a sale. Had it on my followed list for ages and I'm glad to have finally given it a chance. Also, ♥♥♥♥ Bethesda for how they targeted the developer.

Um jogo muito bacana
Praey for the Gods é um jogo inspirado em Shadow of The Colossus e apenas com isso você já tem um resumo da gameplay, que é muito boa.

Os chefes são carismáticos e divertidos de se derrotar, cada um com seu puzzle, e todos são intuitivos, alguns "exigindo mais experimentação até entender o que tem que fazer" do que outros, mas ainda sim, muito bom.

Em questão das fights, o único ponto negativo é o fato de você não ter nenhuma maneira de saber onde estão os pontos fracos do inimigo, algo que Shadow tinha usando a espada, então as vezes você tem que chutar onde eles estão ou futucar todas as partes do corpo do boss até encontrar cordas (que indicam o local aproximado)

Além do combate, o jogo tem um sistema semelhante a Zelda Breath of the Wild onde você vaga, looteia, caça, crafta equipamentos e cozinha, se preparando para a próxima batalha. É uma ideia bem interessante, mas no geral, é meio cru e é possível completar o jogo sem focar nesses aspectos, nem mesmo comendo ou dormindo para ganhar bonus de barras de stamina

Um dos dois únicos pontos realmente negativos é a movimentação crua dá personagem, muitas vezes você spamma para ela agarrar em algo, mas ela não agarra, fazendo-o cair dos chefes, ou um problema que fica bem aparente na reta final do jogo: Ela desliza demais

Em muitos momentos, em chãos que nem são muito íngremes ela desliza sem a opção de agarrar, podendo acabar com uma fight ou resetando ela, tendo que reescalar o monstro. Esse problema é bem aparente na reta final do jogo onde (sem dar spoiler) você tem que andar por o que podemos chamar de "pontes", é um caminho que você TEM que ir, é obrigatório e é o caminho certo, mas mesmo assim ela tem dificuldade em subir nessas pontes e desliza por elas de maneira bugada.

O ultimo problema é o possivel soft lock que você pode sofrer no final, caso você faça uma coisa que inicie a reta final, não tem mais volta e se você não salvou, estará preso nessa reta que é uma boss rush sendo que, a ultima fight você PRECISA do gancho, caso você tenha quebrado todos e não tenha mais madeira para construir outros, eu realmente não sei como alguém conseguiria terminar essa run sem voltar em um save anterior. Não só isso, a cada boss derrotado nessa run, o jogo é salvo junto com sua vida atual, então, se você terminou um boss com pouquissima vida, você terá que enfrentar todos os ultimos com um risco de vida sem chance de recuperar, o que pode ser frustrante, porque para chegar em cada um você tem que passar por uma parte de parkour bem longa, e ter que repetir isso toda vez que o inimigo te acertar 1 golpe é cansativo

De um jeito ou de outro, os lados negativos não sobrepões os positivos, é um otimo, divertido e atmosférico jogo. Espero ansioso uma possível continuação

Praey of the Gods claramente é um jogo inspirado no clássico SOTC (Shadow of the Collossus) sinceramente este jogo me surpreendeu muito, os devs dele sem dúvidas representaram com muita maestria a nostalgia de SOTC, papo de fã mesmo, a única crítica que tenho a fazer é a movimentação da personagem, ficou muito feia, parece uma boneca de pano, mas tirando esse detalhe, eu RECOMENDO MUITO a aquisição deste jogo, para mim VALEU CADA CENTAVO!
bom jogo, é mais trabalhoso executar as ações de derrotar os bichos doq descobrir oq fazer para derrota-los.

Baseando-se em Shadow of the Colossus ou não, eu estou aqui para a experiência que o jogo apresenta, e para mim, ela não foi boa.

Os controles são essencialmente idênticos aos do clássico do PS2, e nisso, não tenho muito a comentar. Simplesmente funciona. Mas isso não justifica a movimentação da personagem ser extremamente travada e muitas vezes não responsiva.

Eu joguei até iniciar a luta contra o terceiro chefe, e bem, eu quase desisti antes disso quando, no segundo chefe, ele simplesmente não morria, mesmo eu tendo acertado completamente todos os pontos fracos dele. E isso não é apenas para o chefe, houveram outros seres pelo mundo também imortais não importava o quanto eu os atacasse.

Além disso, o mundo não é divertido de se explorar, e não é interessante até onde eu tinha visto. As músicas não são ruins na minha visão, mas também não são marcantes.

Não tive a chance de me aprofundar no sistema de criação de equipamento e sobrevivência, mas sendo sincero, o jogo não me prendeu a ponto para tanto.

Por isso, não posso recomendar esse jogo.
Good game

Praey for the Gods claramente nasceu inspirado em Shadow of the Colossus. Ele não tenta esconder isso, e sinceramente? Isso não é um problema nem um pouco.
As batalhas contra os chefes são facilmente a melhor parte do jogo. Escalar criaturas gigantes, procurar pontos fracos e enfrentar esses colossos continua sendo uma ideia absurda de boa.
O problema é que o jogo parece não confiar só nisso. Parece ter tentado misturar um pouco de Zelda BoTW no meio, e por mais que BotW seja incrível e SotC também, a combinação não se torna algo tão agradável... Pelo menos não da forma que eles fizeram aqui!
Os elementos de sobrevivência acabam mais atrapalhando do que ajudando. Frio, fome, crafting… nada disso adiciona muito à experiência. Na verdade, em vários momentos só quebra o ritmo daquilo que realmente importa: as batalhas.
Pra mim, Praey for the Gods seria um jogo muito melhor se tivesse focado quase exclusivamente nos chefes, exatamente como o principal jogo que o inspirou.
Dito isso… vale a pena conhecer.
Mesmo com limitações e algumas escolhas questionáveis, ainda existe algo especial ali. E considerando o preço dele, acho que entrega uma experiência bem válida pra quem curte esse estilo de aventura e escala gigantesca, principalmente se o jogo estiver em promoção!
E eu estou comentando isso anos depois de ter jogado, na esperança desse estúdio voltar a fazer algo novo, e dessa vez, focando somente no que importa!

There's a fine game if you can get past the awkward name.  Praey for the Gods isn't shy about its influences: Shadow of the Colossus, Breath of the Wild, and a hint of a Princess Mononoke vibe, all in a Fimbulwinter sort of scenario.  The catch with paying homage to some serious masterpieces is you're doomed to be constantly compared to some real heavy hitters.  While I wouldn't Praey for the Gods on the same pedestal held by the games it pays homage to, it's a competent entry that is able to stand on its own and does a lot more right than wrong.  If you've enjoyed said influences, you really ought to give it a shot.

Being the gaming masochist I am, and hearing others call the game a tad on the easy side, I started on the hardest difficulty and full survival settings and kept both there throughout.  I can certainly see where others are coming from if they played on lower settings but I'm not about to fault a game for being accessible and you can change difficulty whenever you want so don't be shy about cranking that up if you're not feeling it otherwise.

To be clear, the difficulty mainly comes from the survival gauges, which degrade faster than they really ought to.  Getting hungry and tired while trying to scale a boss is a bad time, as you won't be able to take advantage of the rare opportunities to recoup stamina.  By the same token, snow storms are just plain obnoxious and come up more frequently than they probably should, to include during any boss fight that takes place outdoors, which is most of them.  It's certainly dramatic when that happens though and satisfying to overcome.  Managing the gauges forces you to spend time hunting for resources and building a stockpile of items to see you through the next boss battle and really ups the run time.  Having to stock up and prepare to fight a living high rise that wants to kill you makes sense though.  Health and clothes would be entirely irrelevant, were it not for the freezing damage that can outright kill you on higher levels.  The undead that pop up occasionally aren't really a threat and frankly are more scarce than I'd have liked.  They feel a bit like an afterthought.  Swapping some snow storm frequency for more minion combat would have been nice.

There are plenty of little puzzles, secrets, and lore scattered around an interesting environment of frozen ruins and giant shackled figures, and while most gear doesn't make a huge difference, they provide enough reward to make exploring to find them feel worth it.  The big piece of equipment that stands out is what amounts to the hook shot from many of the Zelda games. Despite being popularized by the franchise, even Breath of the Wild was too cowardly to include it in its open world, so it's quite nice to be able to grapple around and take the edge off of a lot of the climbing, plus it adds some interesting options for boss fights.  By the same token, the paraglider cloth, more or less straight Breath of the Wild, is a very welcome addition to scaling giant bosses.  Using them in tandem? Very good times.

What the game really does right is a lot of the little things.  I mentioned adjustable difficulty already.  Key remapping is there and works like a charm.  I played with mouse and keyboard and had no troubles with anything, thanks to being able to set it up how I like.  The often changing direction of the wind matters not only for the sail cloth but it can slow you down on foot walking into it and you'll put your arm up to shield your face when doing so.  Crafting, repairing and eating all have animations rather than Skyrim-style "open the menu and eat all the cheese".  Beyond good aesthetics, it forces you to be deliberate in minding your gauges and resources, and when you recover.  A good thing in my book. Being able to whittle a bundle of arrows from wood basically any time is also really nice.  Your gear changes appearance as you upgrade it.  Snow is deep in places and slows you down.  You, enemies, animals and even fallen items leave depressions in it as you trudge through, which is a great detail.  Warming your hands near a fire, limping and coughing when seriously hurt, shaky aim when freezing, all good little touches I appreciate.

I'll leave off on a big one.  To the game's immense credit, and despite the bosses being literally numbered, you can fight them in any order, save for the first and final ones in their respective places.  No baloney gatekeeping, no broken cutscenes, no screwed up narrative or progression: if you find it, you can fight it, and you can kill it.  The world actually is open.  Bumbling into a boss while exploring happened more than a few times and I love that it's just a thing you can do, few games allow that.  I wound up defeating them pretty wildly out of order: 1, 2, 4, 6, 5, 3, 7, and 8.

Like I said at the top, Praey for the Gods does a whole lot right and while it's not perfect, it's certainly worth your time.  It's not like "giant boss climber" is a very populated genre and it's been a hot minute since Shadow of the Colossus graced the PS2 so if you have any love in your heart for said genre, or curiosity, in the case of having missed out on such a classic, Praey for the Gods is a worthy entry.  Apparently it came out of a Kickstarter too, so it's really nice to see a quality project rise through a crowdfunding channel, you can tell the developers had passion.

Joguei Praey for the Gods e posso dizer que foi uma experiência incrível. O jogo lembra muito Shadow of the Colossus, e isso pra mim já é um baita elogio. Ele consegue prender do começo ao fim, com uma atmosfera imersiva e um mundo que passa aquela sensação de solidão e desafio constante.

A dificuldade é bem equilibrada — não chega a ser injusta, mas também não é fácil, o que torna cada vitória ainda mais satisfatória. Os colossos são muito bem feitos e as batalhas são empolgantes. Claro, ainda acho que ficam um pouco abaixo de Shadow of the Colossus, mas isso não tira o mérito do jogo, que entrega combates memoráveis e criativos.

Outro ponto que gostei bastante foi a ambientação: o clima gelado, a trilha sonora e a sensação de sobrevivência dão um toque especial à experiência. Explorar o mapa, lidar com o frio e enfrentar criaturas gigantes deixa tudo mais tenso e envolvente.

No geral, é um jogo que vale muito a pena, principalmente pra quem é fã de desafios e de experiências no estilo de Shadow of the Colossus. Recomendo demais!
Boss fights insanas demais, foi bom ter zerado o jogo, vale a pena demais.

Quería jugarlo hace tiempo y recién en los últimos días aproveché las ofertas para comprarlo. Pero antes de jugarlo me platiné Shadows Of The Colossus de PS2 en RetroAchievements para tener la experiencia completa de alguien que le sacó todo el jugo al juego que (lo mires por donde lo mires) se nota que se inspiraron. Y tengo que decír que Praey For The Gods me encantó.

Habiendolo jugado directamente en dificultad Legendaria-Supervivencia tengo que decir que se siente como una extensión muy acorde a lo que uno esperaría para un entorno como el que te presentan. Me encantaron los entornos helados, me encantó sentir la presión de "tengo que vigilar mi calor porque si no pierdo salud pero tengo comidas que me llenan demasiado la barra de salud y no tengo tanta hambre como para estar comiendo esto". Y situaciones como esas, en medio de una pelea de boss, me quemó el bocho... pero me encantó. También es cierto que cuando le encontras la vuelta a organizarte los tiempos, se vuelve un poco más fácil. Pero no tanto. Y eso me gusta. No es algo que dejas relegado, es algo que está ahí, todo el tiempo.

También es cierto que las mecánicas relativas a la supervivencia se sienten un poco cortas ya que estas limitado a la caza y la cocina pero creo que es lo correcto para un juego que no quiere que te quedes quieto sino que busca que te muevas continuamente por el mapa. No viniste a hacer tu casita, no es necesario que la construyas.

Las peleas en tierra con enemigos de tu tamaño se sienten un poco pobres (hablo de los no muertos) pero las peleas contra los bosses resultan bastante satisfactorias cuando le encontras la vuelta y todo empieza a salir bien. Y sí, es cierto lo que dicen de que las 2 ultimas peleas son algo tediosas, es algo que no puedo negar. Pero es como en cualquier juego, si algo no te sale, es porque no le encontraste la vuelta.

Resumen, me encantó, a ver si me lo platino en estos días...

I regret not heading the warnings in other reviews. Praey for the Gods has a stellar premise, but the execution falls flat. The difficulty scaling is artificial; it feels like the developers decided that making a climb take longer was the same thing as making it more difficult. There are various survival and combat mechanics included, but they feel like afterthoughts. They aren't required for boss fights or general progression, leaving you with a gameplay loop that consists of nothing but walking to a boss and climbing it. It’s a letdown for such a cool concept. Honestly if i was to give it stars, it would be a solid 2/10.

The game starts off very enjoyable and the first boss, while a learning curve, is easy to beat. However, because the game is an open world adventure, there is little to no guidance on which boss to fight next. On top of that, the third boss is extremely buggy. I'm constantly clipping through it, the climbing mechanic is glitchy and when I try to climb around on it I fall off, in the middle of a climb, and not when its shaking, its just random. 

I really wanted to like and enjoy this game, as I have many other platformers and boss climbers, but on NORMAL difficulty, doing Story mode, I felt like the game was actively working against its own mechanics working.

In the start I was actually really pulled in by the atmosphere and scale of the world and the bosses. Seeing that there were some treasure hunting to be done I got really optimistic as I'm usually a sucker for collectibles and earning achievements. It was disappointing to realise that the pace of which this game is running ruined my enjoyment and the whole experience. The bells did this.

Boss designs are insane with nice variety and original ideas, one of which gave me actual chills when it flew over me while I was exploring. 
Nice open world with little to no hand holding.
Interesting story which could have used some more dialogue. Maybve, if they had halved the number of bells in the game they could've hired someone to voice the main character.

That being said, the time I've spent on this game has felt like the longest 10 hours of my life.
The theme with the bells is a nice story component that absolutely should have a part in the boss battles, but in my opinion it just shouldn't be ALL you're doing in EVERY boss fight. BELLS, BELLS and MORE BELLS.

Luckily, you can engage in combat with regular enemies out in the world, finally making use of your swords and axes. There are even slightly more difficult enemies called Champions to be found in certain areas. 

I fought my first champion after boss 3, already feeling like "ringing the bell" was getting stale. Realising I had to actually use my weapons to fight him, I was pumped. Maybe the whole game WASN'T just about ringing the bells? 

After landing a number of hits on the champion, he was staggered and fell to his knees. 

That's when I saw the bell on his back.

BELL/10, would ring again if I had literally nothing to do

It works at times, the visuals and music make rather epic and memorable moments.

The developers made a good observation: Breath of the Wild could flow into Shadow of Colossus pretty organically. And when you think about it, those two have some things in common. 

But of course, the devs didn't have the resources of Sony or Nintendo to build a game of their scale and production value. So it's like a cocktail of both of the games, but with some buts and excepts, also lack of the scope, polish, visual details etc.

And here's the thing. You either played those two and it feels like you are doing things you've done before, but the games were much more impressive. Or you haven't. But then, you should probably find a way to play them instead, as you are missing out on some of the best experiences out there.

В декабре 2022 года прошел эту игру, написал обзор для друзей, сейчас решил выложить для всех:
Механики игры — это смесь из игр "Shadow of the Colossus", "The Legend of Zelda" и "The Long Dark", могу ошибаться с точностью названий, т.к. ни в одну из этих игр я не играл (только по Long Dark смотрел нарезку летсплеев), а сужу по отзывам других игроков.
Сюжет у меня оставил больше вопросов, чем дал ответов, мое мнение об игре он не испортил, она мне нравится, как и сам сюжет, хотя мне и хотелось бы чего-то более "конкретного", но, возможно, и для такого "формата сюжета" найдутся поклонники, когда игра даёт не что-то готовое «от и до», а простор для фантазии, теорий и т.д. самого игрока. И, если что, это не я тупой и не понял сюжета, он действительно такой и так преподнесен. Я искал хоть какую-то информацию в т.ч. в англоязычных источниках и везде только догадки и предположения, из которых мне запомнилось, как люди связывают это со скандинавской мифологией, но это все же всего лишь догадки некоторых пользователей, которые строились ещё на раннем доступе игры, в которую потом добавили ещё боссов и ещё сюжета и, как мне кажется, это тот случай, когда не стоило выкладывать игру в раннем доступе, т.к. это не пошло на пользу ни критике игры, ни ее (впоследствии) низкой популярности, ни построению в ней фанатского сообщества.
Многие почему-то (по разным причинам, которые для меня либо не релевантны, либо были актуальны для ранней версии игры) раскритиковали игру, а мне понравилась, не столько сюжетом (как мне кажется, он тут есть), сколько геймплеем, механиками и возможностями игры, это, кстати 1 игра, в которой я сразу начал играть на среднем (нормальном) уровне сложности, а не на лёгком, ибо так интересней, ну и, как выяснилось позже, разница в них небольшая, но, во время ее выбора в начале игры, в описании видны отличия.
В общем, мне игра понравилась, советую, если не играли в упомянутые выше игры, вам тоже, скорее-всего, понравится, а, возможно, я просто, не "искушённый" всякими "Dark Souls'ами" игрок, и поэтому мне понравилось.

[h1] Rating: 6.5-7/10 - recommend on sale [/h1]
[h2] Perfect for any Shadow of the Colossus enjoyers [/h2]

[h3] The good stuff: [/h3]
+ The bosses are all pretty fun and unique. Each of them felt like solving a different type of puzzle, and the devs really nailed the sense of scale and grandiose you experience when fighting the titans, you can really feel the weight and power of their movements and seeing the environment be destroyed as you fight them is really cool. Climbing up their bodies to find the weak spot while fighting to stay on is very reminiscent of SOTC, and still feels just as epic.

+ The boss designs are really cool and adding norse mythology/symbolism to the game is a nice spin on the theme compared to SOTC. Definitely helps the game stick out.

+ The design of the fights themselves is also good. I liked how the game gave you different approaches to fight the bosses and let you use the environment around you to your advantage. Adding some lore notes before each of the fights giving you hints on how to approach the encounters is also a nice touch.

+ The additional movement options (Grapple hook and glider) are really fun and feel very satisfying to use, especially the grapple hook. Being able to switch from the glider to the grapple hook and aim midair as you are falling to catch yourself feels amazing and I really enjoyed that mechanic. I also liked how they were incorporated to help with the boss fights

+ Devs did great adding some QOL features. Having the option to turn off certain aspects of gameplay you dont enjoy and fine-tune the difficulty is nice, especially being able to lessen the survival aspect of the game for those who are more interested in the boss fights. Photo mode is a cool touch, and adding 4 separate controller layouts to pick and choose from helps make the game a lot more accessible to a wider audience.

[h3] The not-so-good stuff: [/h3]
- Survival mechanics felt very tacked on, and although I didn't mind them at first, I think the rate at which your hunger, exhaustion and heat meters drop is way too quick and unmanageable. It felt more like an annoyance that forced you to stop every minute to gather resources rather than a mechanic to encourage the players to be resourceful. Luckily you can mostly turn off the survival aspects of the game in the difficulty menu, but still their addition feels a little unecessary.

- Although, IMO, the gameplay is nowhere near as janky as others make it out to be, the character movement sometimes feels a bit "airy", where your character just kind of drifts along surfaces and slips in certain slopes. Although I understand having your character struggle to stand still while fighting the giants is part of the immersion, sometimes it felt like your character ragdolled too easily and it could get a bit annoying.

- Story is quite confusing, very cryptic like SOTC, but I found myself even more confused. I still did not understand exactly what we did, who we were and what are the wolf and spirit children. Although spreading lore around through letters is a cool concept and I don't mind stories where the player has to piece out the events themselves, this time around I just felt confused and barely invested, even compared to SOTC.

- Travelling through the map is very tedious, even with the added movement options. I wish they incorporated a fast travel system, or a mount system like in SOTC (still a little disappointed the wolf didn't become our mount like Agro was). It would have proved very useful considering this game has a bigger focus on exploration compared to SOTC, and the backtracking you have to do to reach some bosses.

[h3] Final thoughts: [/h3]
If you are a fan of Shadow of the Colossus, this game definitely scratches that itch for a similar experience. The bosses were all fun and had some creative level-design that helped them feel unique from each other. Although the survival mechanics feel quite tacked on and a little unecessary, turning them off is mostly possible through the difficulty menu. The grapple hook and glider are also cool additions and help the gameplay feel a bit more snappy compared to SOTC. The production quality is obviously not on par with SOTC, but for a team of only 3 people this game is quite impressive and a fun experience!
